'''''Star Wars Anthology Series'''''{{SW|url=news/rogue-one-details-revealed-at-star-wars-celebration-anaheim|text=''Rogue One'' Details Revealed at ''Star Wars'' Celebration Anaheim}} is the banner title for a series of stand-alone ''[[Star Wars]]'' films, beginning with ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'' in [[December]] [[2016]]. It was first announced at [[Celebration Anaheim (2015)|Celebration Anaheim]] on [[April 19]], [[2015]]. ==Development== ===Origins=== {{Quote|It's certainly exciting as a filmmaker, the notion that we can explore these stories that genuinely have a beginning, middle and an end, and don't necessarily have to tie into something specific.|[[Kathleen Kennedy]]|{{WebCite|url=http://www.ew.com/article/2016/11/22/rogue-one-lucasfilm-new-star-wars-movies|text=Star Wars: Secret plans for new movies discussed after Rogue One|author=Anthony Breznican|date=2016-11-22|archivedate=20230404011637}}}} In [[April]] [[2012]], five months before [[Lucasfilm]] was sold to [[The Walt Disney Company]], ''[[Star Wars]]'' creator [[George Lucas]] and producer [[Kathleen Kennedy]] sat to talk about the future of ''Star Wars''. In one of their conversations, Lucas told Kennedy that he was planning to retire from blockbuster films and was going to focus on smaller and independently budgeted features, but he told her about the possibility of making more films centered in various characters from the ''Star Wars'' universe.{{WebCite|url=https://www.slashfilm.com/kathleen-kennedy-interview|text=Interview : Lucasfilm Head Kathleen Kennedy Talks About The Future of 'Star Wars'|author=Sciretta, Peter|date=2015-12-17|work=[[Wikipedia:/Film|/Film]]|archivedate=20181109132234}} Screenwriter [[Lawrence Kasdan]] was hired to write a [[Han Solo]]-centric film: "And when I got there, they said, here we have nine ideas. And those were George's ideas. And I said, well I'm not sure I wanna do this. I've really done a lot of Star Wars. And they said, but look, one of these is Han Solo. I said, well okay. I do love Han Solo."{{WebCite|url=https://www.slashfilm.com/lawrence-and-jonathan-kasdan-interview-solo|text=Lawrence and Jonathan Kasdan on Writing Han Solo's Origin and Figuring Out the Kessel Run [Interview]|author=Sciretta, Peter|date=2018-05-25|archivedate=20181203173008}} (After Disney purchased Lucasfilm, he turned his attention to [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']].{{WebCite|url=http://www.slashfilm.com/george-lucas-han-solo-movie|text=Han Solo Movie Was in Development With George Lucas and Lawrence Kasdan Before Disney Bought Lucasfilm|author=Evangelista, Chris|date=2018-02-12|work=[[Wikipedia:/Film|/Film]]|archivedate=20180422112758}}) ===After the Disney deal=== {{Quote|And it's a challenging kind of thing to write, it's something that — you know, everybody wants to write a Star Wars movie, every filmmaker who comes at it, you can see them literally throwing themselves at Kathy like, "Give me a Star Wars." And I've found that they're surprised by just how tricky a sound it is to hit.|[[Jon Kasdan]]|{{SW|url=news/solo-lawrence-and-jonathan-kasdan-interview|text=A Portrait of the Scoundrel as a Young Man: Writers Lawrence and Jonathan Kasdan on ''Solo: A Star Wars Story''|author=Dan Brooks|date=2018-05-24}}}} News that the Disney-Lucasfilm brand was developing several theatrical pictures separate from the core, episodic ''[[Star Wars]]'' saga was reported in [[2013]], with Lawrence Kasdan and [[Simon Kinberg]] slated to write their own individual spinoff films.{{SW|url=news/new-spinoff-films-set-to-expand-the-star-wars-galaxy|text=New Spinoff Films Set to Expand the ''Star Wars'' Galaxy}} While director [[Gareth Edwards]]' then-untitled [[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story|''Rogue One'']] project was announced in [[2014]] as the first of these standalone features,{{SW|url=news/gareth-edwards-and-gary-whitta-onboard-for-star-wars-stand-alone-film|text=Gareth Edwards and Gary Whitta Onboard for ''Star Wars'' Stand-Alone Film}} it was not until the [[2015|following year]] on [[April 19]] at [[Celebration Anaheim (2015)|Celebration Anaheim]] that the announcement was made that the spinoff films would collectively be known as the ''Star Wars Anthology Series''. [[Josh Trank]] signed on to direct an Anthology film in [[2014]] but left the project after a year to pursue other opportunities.{{SW|url=news/josh-trank-departs-star-wars-anthology-film|text=Josh Trank Departs ''Star Wars'' Anthology Film}} On [[July 7]], [[2015]], Lawrence Kasdan's Anthology film was given a release date of [[May 25]], [[2018]], with [[Christopher Miller]] and [[Phil Lord]] attached to direct, and Kasdan's son [[Jon Kasdan]] contributing to the script as well. The film would follow the story of a young [[Han Solo]]. On [[June 20]], [[2017]], it was announced that Lord and Miller were stepping away from the project.{{SW|url=news/a-message-from-lucasfilm-regarding-the-untitled-han-solo-film|text=A Message from Lucasfilm Regarding the Untitled Han Solo Film}} on [[June 22]], it was announced [[Ron Howard]] would assume directorial duties on the film. ===Future projects=== In [[July]] [[2015]], director [[Guillermo del Toro]], who was at one point considered to direct [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']], commented that he pitched an idea for a film about [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]],{{WebCite|url=https://nerdist.com/guillermo-del-toro-wants-to-make-star-wars-jabba-the-hutt-origin-film|text=Guillermo Del Toro Wants to Make Star Wars: Jabba the Hutt Origin Film|author=Marnell, Blair|date=2015-07-13|work=Nerdist|archivedate=20180616062307}} and in [[2017]], it was reported that the idea was one of the many projects considered by Lucasfilm Ltd.{{WebCite|url=https://screenrant.com/star-wars-jabba-hutt-movie|text=Star Wars: Jabba the Hutt Spinoff Being Considered By Lucasfilm|author=Hood, Cooper|date=2017-08-18|work=Screen Rant|archivedate=20190203175644}}{{WebCite|url=https://news.avclub.com/you-will-soon-learn-to-appreciate-the-jabba-the-hutt-sp-1798346181|text=You will soon learn to appreciate the Jabba the Hutt spin-off in development|author=Chavez, Danette|date=2017-08-18|work=A.V. Club|archivedate=20191208155911}} In [[August]] [[2017]], several sources rumored that a film focusing on [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] was in development, with [[Stephen Daldry]] in negotiations to direct it and with [[Ewan McGregor]] potentially reprising his role. This film later became the [[Star Wars: Obi-Wan Kenobi|''Obi-Wan Kenobi'']] television series that streams on [[Disney+]]. It was also reported that Lucasfilm was considering various spin-off films focused on many beloved ''[[Star Wars]]'' characters like [[Boba Fett]] or [[Jedi Master]] [[Yoda]].{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/obi-wan-kenobi-star-wars-film-planned-director-talks-1030505|text='Star Wars' Obi-Wan Kenobi Film in the Works (Exclusive)|author=Kit, Borys|date=2017-08-17|work=The Hollywood Reporter|archivedate=20200505213215}}{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2017/film/news/obi-wan-kenobi-star-wars-movie-disney-stephen-daldry-1202531346|text='Star Wars' Obi-Wan Kenobi Movie in Early Development at Disney|author=Kroll, Justin|date=2017-08-17|work=Variety|archivedate=20200308132134}} In September 2018, Bob Iger told ''The Hollywood Reporter'' that Lucasfilm had reevaluated its release schedule for future films: "I made the timing decision, and as I look back, I think the mistake that I made — I take the blame — was a little too much, too fast. You can expect some slowdown, but that doesn't mean we're not gonna make films. J.J. [Abrams] is busy making [Episode] IX. We have creative entities, including [''Game of Thrones'' creators David] Benioff and [D.B.] Weiss, who are developing sagas of their own, which we haven't been specific about. And we are just at the point where we're gonna start making decisions about what comes next after J.J.'s. But I think we're gonna be a little bit more careful about volume and timing. And the buck stops here on that."{{WebCite|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/bob-iger-disneys-streaming-service-james-gunn-star-wars-slowdown-1145493|text=Bob Iger Talks Disney's Streaming Service, 'Roseanne,' James Gunn and a Coming 'Star Wars' "Slowdown"|author=Belloni, Matthew|date=2018-09-20|work=The Hollywood Reporter|archivedate=20200803070114}} According to production designer [[Neil Lamont]], when the announcement was made, his team was working on a spin-off that involved [[Tatooine]].{{WebCite|url=https://www.cinemablend.com/news/2455795/star-wars-production-designer-confirms-tatooine-was-part-of-an-upcoming-spin-off-film|text=Star Wars Production Designer Confirms Tatooine Was Part Of An Upcoming Spin-Off Film|author=Eisenberg, Eric|date=15-08-2018|work=[[Wikipedia:Cinemablend|Cinemablend]]|archivedate=20200610101214}} ''[[Star Wars: Andor]]'' was retroactively retitled 'Andor: A Star Wars Story' in [[Andor Season 2|its second season]]. {{SW|url=news/andor-season-2-teaser-trailer-key-art-reveal|text=First ''Andor A Star Wars Story'' Teaser Trailer and Poster Revealed}} ==Media== ===Films=== {| class="wikitable plainrowheaders" style="text-align:center; width:95%" |- !Image !
